text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysia is introducing tough new regulations on chemicals imports to prevent dumping of hazardous substances by developed nations.

-- Malaysia's national oil company, Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) is expected to post a record profit in the year to March 31, 1997, according to its chairman Azizan Zainul Abidin. He did not provide any details in the interview in Montreal.
-- New bond issues picked up in March, this year, according to the Rating Agency Malaysia (RAM). It said the amount rose to 2.48 billion ringgit against 1.52 billion in the month before.

-- Malaysia is expected to become self-reliant in cement production by 1999. Malayan Cement Bhd Managing Director Jeffery C. Pope said the cement industry had imported 700,000 tonnes in the first four months of this year. Peninsular Malaysia's total consumption last year was 13.3 million tonnes.
-- Malaysia's Pahang State Development Corp has signed a 250 million ringgit revolving credit facility with a nine-bank consortium led by Standard Chartered Bank.
